title: Lionsgate Is Open to Another Hunger Games Movie
excerpt:
Film chief Adam Fogelson wants to work with Suzanne Collins again.
No additional installment has been officially announced.
body_md:
The success of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping has renewed interest in the franchise's future. The film opened at number one with $119.3 million from 4,018 North American locations, outperforming the previous two installments' opening weekends.

Lionsgate Motion Picture Group chair Adam Fogelson expressed enthusiasm for another collaboration with Suzanne Collins, while emphasizing that the author should determine the next story. He is prepared to read another project whenever Collins is ready and intends to wait for her decision.

Directed by Francis Lawrence with a reported $150 million budget, the prequel stars Joseph Zada as young Haymitch Abernathy, previously portrayed by Woody Harrelson. Its story unfolds 24 years before the events of the original novel.

The 2023 prequel, The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes, opened to $44 million domestically and ultimately earned $361.8 million worldwide. Fogelson explained that its villain-origin premise presented a different commercial challenge. Fan interest in Haymitch's history encouraged the studio to invest more heavily in the latest production.

The Sunrise on the Reaping novel sold 1.5 million copies in its first week. Fans have suggested additional stories within the dystopian universe, but it remains uncertain whether any will inspire Collins to write another book. Lionsgate's enthusiasm is clear; a seventh film, its storyline and release date have not been officially announced.
